profile.headline: Software Engineer Manager
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
I focus on formal Knowledge Representation and Reasoning applied to discovery, data Integration, and data curation. My main research topic is efficient algorithms for logical reasoning, and I have experience in Machine Learning and Information Extraction topics. In the last years I have served as technology lead in projects focused on knowledge management, integration and reasoning. 

The topic of my Ph.D. dissertation was efficient query-rewriting-based reasoning techniques for OWL2 QL and SPARQL. I also lead a team in the development of -ontop-, a system that implements the ideas behind my dissertation (e.g., reasoning on virtual graphs, efficient mapping manipulation, efficient rewritings). The system is still ongoing. Since its first release,  several for profit and public projects have adopted/integrated -ontop- as reasoning engine including, well known commercial triple store, research projects in private companies, EU projects (e.g., the Optique project).

positions.title: Researcher
positions.description: Researcher in Semantic Web Technologies, High performance reasoning, Logics and Databases and in general, semantic data integration. In the last years I have served as Technology Lead in several medium (5 people) and large projects (20 people), defining strategies and coordinating execution on the Knowledge Representation, Reasoning and Management aspects of these projects. While in IBM I have also worked and learned on topics related knowledge management such as Information Extraction, NLP, consistency checking, vectorial representations for text and graphs.

positions.title: Tech lead
positions.description: Tech lead on large Knowledge Representation and Reasoning project with a major IBM client. The focus was on use of KR and Reasoning for the data integration needs of the client. Role involves setting the research and development strategy and carrying out the execution with a team of developers and researchers.

positions.title: Researcher
positions.description:
I am an researcher at the KRDB research center. Following up on my Ph.D. topics, I focus on the optimisation of rewriting based techniques for query answering over OWL ontologies and relational databases. I lead a small group (4 people) in the development of the -ontop- framework for OBDA, a system in which all our research is implemented and which is currently one of the fastest SPARQL engines that supports virtual RDF graphs over RDBMS and the only one with support for RDFS and OWL entailments. 

Other responsibilities of this position include teaching and tutoring. I am responsible for teaching the masters course on  Semantic Web Technologies since 2009, and I the Knowledge Bases and Databases laboratories since 2007. Since 2007, I have supervised 5 student projects, 2 bachelor theses and 5 master theses, all related to OBDA and Semantic Web techniques or applications.

positions.title: Visiting Researcher
positions.description: I visited the Center for Biomedical Informatics Research to work on the topics Ontology Based Data Access with Paea LePendu and Matthew Horridge.

positions.title: PhD student
positions.description: I carried out my Ph.D. on the topic of "Efficient Query Answering by Query Rewriting over DL-Lite ontologies" under the supervision of Prof. Diego Calvanese. Topics covered in this work included the application of Semantic Query Optimisation techniques for the optimisation of query rewriting techniques, experimentation with different forms of SQL query rewriting and the development of the first prototype for an efficient query answering system for DL-Lite ontologies over arbitrary relational DBMS.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Freelance developer at the Rent-A-Coder site. During this period I implemented diverse projects for several clients contacted trough this website. The projects ranged from simple scripts for doing data analytics over CSV or SQL databases, to the development of websites using diverse technologies. Languages and systems involved in these projects included: Java, PHP, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Bash,  HTML, Flash, Excel and Photoshop.

projects.title: Optique
projects.description:
Optique is a large-scale integrating project (IP) of the FP7 framework. The objective of Optique is to bring about a paradigm shift for data access by i) providing a semantic end-to-end connection between users and data sources ii) enabling users to rapidly formulate intuitive queries using familiar vocabularies and conceptualisations ii) seamlessly integrating data spread across multiple distributed data sources, including streaming sources iii) exploiting massive parallelism for scalability far beyond traditional RDBMSs and thus reducing the turnaround time for information requests to minutes rather than days. The project secured 14 million euro financing for a total of 4 years and involves 6 academic partners (Free University of Bolzano, University of Oxford, University of Oslo, Hamburg University of Technology, Sapienza Universita di Roma and the University of Athens) and 4 industrial partners (Siemens, Statoil, fluidOperations and DNV).

I participated in the creation of the project proposal for Optique, in which the techniques I work on, and the system -ontop-, play a central role. I currently lead the team working on Optique at the Free University of Bolzano.

projects.title: -ontop- Framework for Ontology Based Data Access
projects.description: I am the main author and leader of the development team of the -ontop- framework for Ontology Based Data Access. The system consists of several tools and APIs to allow for mapping relational databases to RDF/OWL ontologies, and to query them using SPARQL. It includes Quest, an SPARQL engine based on SPARQL-to-SQL translation techniques that currently outperforms similar systems while providing functionality not available in any other system (e.g., entailment regimes).
